title: Senior professional economist
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Design, implement, and lead programmes of economic analysis to support decision-making.

knowledges.detail: Economic theory, including micro-economic and macro-economic theories, and approaches to their application in analysing and solving complex problems in diverse contexts.
Advanced econometric techniques, such as micro-econometric methods, time series analysis, and panel data analysis, recognising their limitations and the appropriate contexts for their use.
Data quality and robustness, including approaches to assessing the robustness and quality of economic statistics, model-generated data, and external information.

Data visualisation and presentation, including advanced approaches to data visualisation and presentation, and approaches to the use of digital tools and channels to communicate complex information effectively.
Appraisal and evaluation techniques, such as cost-benefit analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, multi-criteria decision analysis, and non-market valuation.

Features of economic models and policy implications, including competing economic models and their implications for policymaking, such as market failures, rationales for intervention, and business strategies.
Quality assurance in analysis, including approaches to developing and implementing quality assurance techniques to identify and mitigate risks to the quality of economic analysis.

The wider context affecting economic analysis, including political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental factors, the broader economics of biodiversity and climate change, and approaches to assessing their impact on stakeholders and analytical outcomes.
Strategic business objectives, including how to formulate and implement high-level business objectives and strategies to anticipate and meet the demands for economic analysis.

behaviours.detail: Demonstrates ethical conduct when carrying out analysis, including attributing sources and ideas to their originators, and provides honest advice on all relevant aspects of an issue while avoiding bias.
Is proactive when solving problems, and seeks ideas for improvements and opportunities to apply analysis within the relevant organisational context.
Advocates for analysis and uses professional judgement to reach conclusions, even when evidence is incomplete.

Works collaboratively, including understanding others' points of view and adapting approaches accordingly, seeks to reconcile different views, builds trust with colleagues and clients, and shares ideas and work with other professionals.

Respects and appreciates diversity by listening to others' points of view, however challenging, inviting and considering feedback, and demonstrating awareness of the impact of language and non-verbal behaviour on others.
Takes a rigorous approach to analysis that strives for accuracy and detail in analytical outputs.
Leads others to deliver economic analysis outcomes.

skills.detail: Apply micro-economic and macro-economic theories and modelling, including econometrics, to inform recommendations for decision-makers.

Analyse policy or other questions by selecting the most appropriate analytical method, including consideration of key economic approaches where appropriate, such as non-market valuation methods, the counterfactual, opportunity cost, risk and uncertainty, and the estimation of discount rates and costs of capital.
Use digital tools and technologies, such as coding, Artificial Intelligence, and software packages, safely and securely, as relevant to the role.

Document, use, record, and store data and information relating to individuals securely and in line with legal and regulatory requirements, and local and national policies, including the safe use of digital technologies.
Carry out data analysis, including cleansing and manipulating data, identifying data limitations, and explaining them to stakeholders.
Use data visualisation techniques to explain concepts and implications to stakeholders to aid their understanding and facilitate decision-making.

Communicate economic principles and concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders, present trade-offs and uncertainties and articulate these clearly, and frame advice, drawing on knowledge of stakeholders' positions, for maximum impact.
Research and critically assess available information sources, and judge their validity and usefulness in responding to economic challenges.
Critically assess economic analysis produced by others and suggest improvements.
Design and implement quality assurance processes, following organisational best practice and drawing on sources of external expertise.
Research and anticipate new trends, opportunities, technologies, and challenges that may influence outcomes of interest to clients.
Build and maintain relationships with stakeholders, including developing and utilising internal and external professional networks.
Deploy project management techniques, including managing delivery risks.
Promote compliance with regulations, legislation, and policies that support and promote equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace.
Identify, analyse, and communicate how impacts may vary across different social groups, including those with protected characteristics.

involvedEmployers: Bank of England, Council of the society of professional economists, Department of Business and Trade, Department of Energy Security , Food Standards Agency (FSA), HM Treasury, HMRC, Institute for Fiscal Studies, OXERA, UKRI

duties.dutyDetail: Analyse stakeholder needs and manage their expectations.
Anticipate analytical requirements and proactively scope potential work programmes for clients and colleagues.
Improve analytical techniques to address economic questions, setting new standards for model performance, such as more accurate or more extensive predictions.
Develop new techniques, or adapt existing ones, when faced with novel analytical questions.
Create or commission appropriate economic models to inform advice and decision-making, including policy and business decisions.
Review and critically evaluate published information, such as literature reviews, reports, statistics, and databases, relevant to the task or project.
Structure, clean, and manipulate data and, where appropriate, design and oversee data collection and transformation. Evaluate results, testing for robust statistical and economic conclusions.
Evaluate weaknesses in the quality of evidence bases, identify data gaps, and develop approaches to addressing them.
Contextualise and adapt analysis, considering relevant wider political, social, economic, and environmental issues.
Build relationships with others and collaborate effectively to deliver high-quality economic analysis that influences and informs decision-making.

Develop and implement strategies to communicate complex economic ideas, arguments, and solutions to senior stakeholders and clients, and provide technical advice and support to technical and non-technical colleagues with influence and impact, using the most effective styles and tools for their needs.
Deliver value-for-money outputs, taking account of trade-offs between the quality of analysis, impact, resources, and time.
Lead approaches to the quality assurance of economic analysis.

Deliver economic analysis services using digital technology safely and securely to protect the organisation from cyber security risks and reputational harm, with an awareness of the benefits and risks to the organisation and its clients.
Source, handle, and store confidential and sensitive information and digital data safely and securely.

Maintain professional knowledge and development, including developments in data science; digital tools, including software packages such as Excel, SPSS, STATA, R, and SAS; and techniques such as behavioural insights.
